messages:
sam: Heads-up: sketching a small playbook for auto-fallback audit + playback. Goal: make it easy for oncall/product to answer "why did this flip" in <2 mins. trying to keep UI minimal.

anya: Love it. What fields do you want visible in the first glance?

sam: Top line: action (auto/fallback/revert), timestamp, saturation_score, primary_signal. expandable row shows full snapshot and a link to playback.

jordan: Playback should be a time-series mini-chart overlay showing p95, error-rate, queue length with the flip marker. super useful for triage.

leah: Also include a one-line quality impact estimate, e.g. "expected latency down 30%, cost down 18%, quality delta TBD". That keeps product in the loop.

mike: For audit entries we need immutable snapshot + compact diff. Example audit JSON (for storage):
```json
{"ts":"2024-04-22T19:33:10Z","policy_id":"pl-23","action":"fallback","score":72,"signals":{"p95_ms":2150,"5xx_rate":0.028,"queue":240},"operator":null,"snapshot_hash":"sha256:..."}
```

psf-bot: note: telemetry will include fallback.playback_url and fallback.audit_id. indexing planned on policy_id and operator.

sam: Retention: we should keep playback-ready telemetry for 30 days by default, archive 1% long-term. Longer retention via export.

anya: How do we avoid noisy flips from cold-starts/regional restarts? Exemptions list?

jordan: Strategy: add policy pre-filters - ignore spikes if origin_hosts_changed>50% in last 2m or if a single host contributes >80% of errors. Also require 2 distinct signals in 90s.

leah: Microcopy for the modal override button: "Hold fallback for 15m (auto-resume)" and "Pin override until next deployment". When an operator clicks, ask for a short reason.

mike: Important: every override creates two telemetry events: fallback.override_request (with reason) and fallback.override_effect (with snapshot post-override). That links intent -> outcome.

sam: Sampling: default audit_sample_rate 1% but burst_capture: upon first policy flip in a 24h window capture 100% for 10m. ops can bump sample rate per-customer.

psf-bot: action: ops ticket created (#INF-842) for burst capture infra changes.

anya: UX question: should the policy editor show a human-friendly builder (toggles/sliders) and an advanced JSON editor?

jordan: Yes. Builder for common cases (latency, error-rate, queue). Advanced for power users. Show the equivalent JSON in read-only beside builder.

leah: On alerts: add a small checkbox "send PagerDuty when auto-fallback triggers" and a short cooldown to avoid alert storms.

mike: For playback API: /v1/policies/{id}/simulate?window=6h returns simulated flip events. We'll make that available to the UI for dry-run and the modal "what-if" preview.

sam: Proposed example policy expression for the builder layer:
```
when (p95_ms > 1200 for 2m AND (5xx_rate > 1.5% for 3m OR queue > 200 for 1m)) then fallback->region-small
cooldown 5m
burst_capture 10m
```

anya: This is great. Can someone prototype the modal with the playback mini-chart next week? I'll wire up copy once we lock the button text.

jordan: I'll take the mini-chart mock and the builder -> JSON mapping.

mike: I'll ship the simulate endpoint and the audit payload shape.

psf-bot: reminder: ensure audit entries are immutable and accessible to legal/compliance requests.

sam: Thanks — if folks can drop edge cases here (single-host spikes, DB failover causing transient errors, traffic skew from A/B experiments) we'll add explicit exceptions to the pre-filter list.
